proven: Read-only local API exposes health, state, claim-state, workspace-status, pass-ledger, workspace-config, workspace-layout, and intake records.
Durable status files are committed product source and parse as JSON.
Browser dashboard renders current pass and source-truth paths from the API.
Default local settings define an app-owned runtime data directory without importing user files.
Metadata-only intake records omit source paths and contents and do not copy, move, delete, extract, execute, or launch source files.
Runtime data resolves through OS user-data conventions or an explicit absolute override and never depends on the source checkout path.
API and dashboard records expose logical location metadata instead of resolved personal filesystem paths.
Every tracked source file has a machine-readable purpose and maintenance record.
Python modules and public components plus frontend and workflow file headers are protected by an explainability verifier.
A durable start guide, architecture guide, file map, and code-explanation standard let a new human or model resume from repository truth.
Validated intake metadata maps deterministically to read-only route previews with planned steps and explicit blockers.
Route previews do not use source paths, read contents, open files, extract archives, execute routes, launch tools, or create outputs.
The dashboard renders route-preview status and candidates without treating preview state as execution readiness.
Route previews map to planned output bundles, expected artifacts, logical destinations, and required proof checklists.
Every output artifact remains planned and nonexistent, every proof item remains not proven, and create/open actions remain blocked.
Output planning exposes only logical app-owned locations and never creates directories, writes files, captures proof, or opens outputs.
Known maker tools are checked through PATH and narrowly scoped standard locations without executing processes or reading the registry.
Tool detection results expose tool identity, family, method, and executable name while withholding resolved installation paths.
Missing matches remain not proven, versions remain not proven, and launch/install/update/uninstall/repair actions remain blocked.
Route previews, output plans, and detected tool families compose into semantic tool dry-run plans.
Dry-run plans use logical source and destination references, select only family-compatible detected tools, and expose no resolved paths.
Dry-run planning constructs no command string, performs no file handoff, launches no process, writes nothing, and remains execution-blocked.
Execution gate policy allowlists only mesh-to-toolpath, reserves one future concurrency slot, and keeps execution disabled.
Gate evaluation distinguishes proven planning evidence from unproven authorization, containment, compatibility, cancellation, logging, and proof requirements.
No execution request is created, no authorization is accepted, no path or command is resolved, and no process or execution-side record is produced.
State-changing API methods remain blocked.
